A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FlashLips and contain complete, readable main papers and appendices A–F. Their text, equations, tables, and rendered figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction and cross-audio experiments, runtime measurements, ablations, qualitative tests, and a user study in Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including Tables 1–5, appendix results, and the user-preference outcomes in Figure C.1.

M1.justification: Table A.3 revises the specified Stage-2 input projection from (12+16)→1024 to 12→1024. This is a limited architecture-specification revision; the PDFs do not establish whether the implementation changed or the table was corrected. The two-stage procedure, losses, and main-text 12D lips representation remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The training collections, HDTF/CelebV-HQ/CelebV-Text evaluations, reconstruction and cross-audio tasks, and appendix pose and synthetic/non-human scenarios are retained. Figure 5 substitutes examples within existing coverage.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain DiffDub, Diff2Lip, TalkLip, LatentSync, IP-LAP, and KeySync. Changes from IP LAP or IP_LAP to IP-LAP are spelling standardization, not comparator changes.

E3.justification: Both versions report the same 100 reconstruction videos and 100 cross-audio pairs, evaluation metrics, training schedules, and user-study procedure. The revised illustrative frames do not establish a changed evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: Figure 5 revises the qualitative cases supporting visual-quality and identity-preservation comparisons: displayed frames change for the left pair, and the right source/driver pair is replaced. The systematic ablations, failure examples, and appendix pose/OOD analyses are unchanged.

E5.justification: Runtime reporting still averages 10 measurements after five warm-ups. Neither version adds seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or another uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Figure 5 contains substituted qualitative outputs, including a different right-hand source/driver pair. Numerical results in Tables 1–5, C.4, and C.5 and user-preference counts in Figure C.1 are unchanged. The replacement examples do not establish a same-setting performance improvement.

T1.justification: The reconstruction and flow-matching equations, loss definitions, and pseudo-pair formulation are unchanged. Table A.3 revises an implementation specification rather than adding theoretical reasoning, assumptions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction explicitly restrict the >100 FPS claim to the U-Net variant. This clarifies their previously generic wording and agrees with the retained Table 2 measurements: 109.41 FPS for U-Net versus 66.84 for the Transformer. Other central contributions remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Interpretations of disentanglement, mask removal, reference-count trade-offs, and backbone trade-offs are retained, as are the limitations involving fine details, occlusions, and VAE artifacts. The added explanation of 'highly conditioned' restates the existing deterministic-editing rationale.

D1.justification: Table A.3 revises the input dimensions and condition-embedding notation and defines d_p as the lips-pose dimension. This improves consistency with the existing 12D description, although the output decoder still uses d_w after its definition is removed. Other implementation and resource disclosures are unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and cited works are unchanged, including the positioning relative to GANs, diffusion methods, and earlier mask-free lip synchronization.

P1.justification: v2 lightly edits the abstract and contributions, standardizes U-Net and IP-LAP terminology, and updates author affiliations. The section order and overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: Figure 3 adds explanatory stage subtitles and adjusts component placement; Figure 4 is compacted. Several figures clarify 'Driver' as 'Driver Audio,' and Figure 5 replaces displayed examples. Table organization and the overall document layout remain substantially the same.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves precision by qualifying the headline speed claim and aligning Table A.3's input dimensions with the existing 12D formulation. Clearer diagram and audio-driver labels also help readers. These gains outweigh the small remaining notation problem in Table A.3, where d_w loses its definition; the empirical conclusions otherwise remain unchanged.
